# Review - PR 579 @ d418467d6b0b9c786284b6639f22fea8a20f9e0d

Independent review by a Claude Opus helper (owner-authorized 2026-09-17); no author, fixer or prior reviewer context reused. Trusted prompt, persona and policy ref: cbb95dc49eebf388180e51d4c46c6b656d63e936. Workflow-layer and documentation change only: 14 files, 2684 insertions / 3 deletions against merge base 7c3f512e (base branch `main`), adding a model-free duplicate-declaration scanner, its CLI and claims registry, a dispatch-time guard, a repository copy of the worker-claim script, protocol prose and one generated sweep report; no Lean statement, definition, blueprint node or gate is touched.

## Findings

- none

## Review

Scope and policy. Trusted policy was read from `github/main` at cbb95dc4 (`local/personas/reviewer.md`, `local/personas/prose-reviewer.md`, `local/protocols/review.md`, `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` section 5, and the proof-integrity and faithful-statement sections of `AGENTS.md`); nothing was read from the branch as policy. The published head d418467d equals the worktree HEAD. Exact-head CI is green: `local-ci/summary` success, with build, blueprint-render, blueprint-sync, paper-gaps, file-length, proof-debt, proof-evasion and statement-origin all success. The branch carries three commits: the feature commit, a merge of current `github/main`, and the review-fix commit; the main-relative diff is the 14 files above.

Proof integrity. `git diff --name-only` against the merge base lists zero `.lean` files and no blueprint TeX, no gate script and no CI configuration; the only `axiom` token added anywhere in the diff is inside the declaration-head regex of `scripts/dup_scan.py`, and no `sorry`, `admit` or `native_decide` appears. The single change to an existing module is the keyword-only `text=` parameter on `scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.collect_file_lean_decls` (default `None`, previous body preserved); I checked every caller in the repository (`blueprint_lean_sync.py:480,924`, `check_source_statement_changes.py:125`, `scripts/tests/test_blueprint_lean_sync.py:373`) and none passes it, so the blueprint-sync and statement-origin gates are unaffected — their green steps at this head agree. Nothing in the new tooling can weaken a statement: it reads blobs with `git show` and prints names. `local/bin/claim.sh` is a faithful copy of the operator script it names; I diffed it against `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/qpbt-claim.sh` and the only changes are the comment header, the `MIPSTARRE_CLAIM_FILE`/`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` indirection, an added `mkdir -p` and the usage string — the awk claim/release semantics, the flock and the on-disk line format are byte-identical.

Prior review. The earlier marked review 5237652764 (head e1f09d31) left four unchecked findings; I re-checked each against this head rather than trusting the fix commit. F1: `_matches_on_ref` no longer short-circuits silently — a new `_unreadable_ref` is consulted first by `check`, `sweep`, `claim`, `claims-check` and `predispatch`. Verified by running the tool in the PR worktree: `claims-check --ref no-such-ref` prints "ref no-such-ref not present locally; duplicate check skipped (this tool never fetches on its own)" and exits 4, the same query against `github/main` still exits 3 with the `file:line`, and `check --ref no-such-ref --json` returns a `skipped` key with exit 4; the "no duplicate" line is no longer printed for an unread ref, and the docstring at `local/bin/dup_check.py:27-33` now states the rule. F2: the headings of `local/protocols/issues-prs.md` now ascend 1-7 (`## 7. Duplicate-work guards` at :306, after `## 6. Owner inbox…` at :257), and no existing section was renumbered, so the four files citing "section 6" still point at the owner-inbox section. F3: the per-PR table now has separate "already on the reference" (distinct matched declarations, new helper `matched_declarations` at `scripts/dup_scan.py:367`) and "matches" columns with a note above the table; no row of the regenerated report exceeds its new-declarations column (#398 reads 200/200/222, #400 reads 7/7/26). F4: the front matter reads `pr: "#579"`.

Code. The scanner reuses `blueprint_lean_sync`'s Lean parser and `strip_lean_comments_preserve_lines` instead of writing a second one, and sits beside `scripts/check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`, the existing textual declaration audit; I found no declaration-index helper on `main` that it duplicates. The synthetic-anchor trick in `decls_from_text` is sound (`collect_file_lean_decls` derives `rel` as `lean_file.relative_to(lean_root.parent)`, and `/dup-scan/<rel>` against `/dup-scan/root` yields `<rel>`), and the `TypeError` guard gives a clear message against an un-upgraded helper. `new_declarations` feeds an already-computed merge base into a `base...head` diff, which is the same commit set. In `dispatch.sh` the guard sits after `die`/`note` (:76,:83), `ISSUE` (:162) and `SCRIPT_DIR`/`REPO_ROOT` (:271-272); the mode word is validated with `die 2`, a missing `dup_check.py`, a non-numeric scope word, exit 4 and any unexpected exit only warn, and only `fatal` plus exit 3 refuses — so the guard cannot silently stop a dispatch, and `DUP_OUT="$(…)" && DUP_RC=0 || DUP_RC=$?` records the real exit code under `set -e`. I ran the four new test modules in the PR worktree with byte-code writing disabled: 55 tests, all passing, fixtures synthetic (temp git repositories, a stub `codex` on PATH, no network, no model), and `git status --porcelain` in the worktree was empty before and after. Two non-blocking observations, neither contradicting the documented behaviour: `predispatch` checks the issue's claimed names only against the ref, not against other issues' open claims, so a claim recorded with `--force` over another issue's claim is re-warned at dispatch only if `main` also has the name (the cross-issue refusal happens at claim time, which is what `issues-prs.md` section 7 describes); and `read_claims` uses `path.read_text()` with the locale default while `append_claim` writes `encoding="utf-8"`.

Prose. The sweep report follows the dated-filename rule and the audit metadata format, its headline (69 examined, 38 flagged, 34 by fully qualified name) matches the 69 table rows, the detail cap arithmetic is right ("and 210 more" for 222 matches with 12 shown), and the Limitations section states the three real caveats plus the skipped-head rule. I independently confirmed one sampled match, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus.stateQForm_zero`, at `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:43` on `github/main`. Section 7 of `issues-prs.md` and the registry README describe the implemented behaviour, including advisory exit 4, `--force` semantics and the separation between declaration claims and worker claims; the `EVOLUTION.md` entry has the Trigger/Change/Expected-effect fields of `local/protocols/meta.md`, and its trigger — the owner decision recorded in issue #576, itself logged in `results/telemetry/events.md` on 2026-09-17 — is one of the triggers standing principle 2 allows, so the protocol amendment is evidence-driven. PR body and commit conventions hold: `type(scope): short description` subjects, Motivation/Description/Testing, and no closing keyword bound to a number in the commit messages.

Not checked. I did not run `lake build`, the pre-commit hook, `ci.sh` or the full test suite (only the four new modules), and no Lean file needed elaboration because none changed. I did not re-run the sweep, so its per-PR counts are checked only for internal consistency and one sampled match. I did not exercise the GitHub reads of `sweep` or `check --pr`, `predispatch` inside a real dispatch against the live registry, or the `--node` blueprint-label path. The committed registry file is empty at this head, so its conflict logic is covered by the unit tests only.

VERDICT: APPROVED (code=APPROVED, prose=APPROVED)
